### What's new since 0.9.5-7

- **Random maps follow the game's templates much more closely**: when you pick a game template, the generator now places the template's mandatory objects in each zone (mines, mana wells, markets, forges, arenas, random-hire buildings and so on) and spends each zone's treasure budgets instead of only biasing the rolls. In a test over all 70 bundled templates, 94% of the mandatory object types now appear (was 42%). The template's own item limits are respected, with the exception of its mandatory entries. Not played in the game yet.
- **The Random Map dialog greys out what a template decides**: with a game template picked, Players and Max heroes show the template's values, and Richness, Complexity and Water are greyed out (Complexity and Water show the closest level, the tooltip gives the template's real number). Difficulty stays selectable.
- **Map Grid: decorations turned 180° or 270° are no longer drawn flipped**, so their baked-in shadow no longer jumps to the wrong side of the light. Mirrored objects are still mirrored.
- Ground shadows now use a lower light angle (40°), and the decoration images were re-rendered to match.

See [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/mimiasei/map-editor-json-tool/compare/v0.9.5-7...v0.9.5-8) for what changed.

### What's new since 0.9.5-6

- **Polish (Polski) interface language**: pick it in the Theme editor. Menus, dialogs, tooltips, guides and templates follow it, and on the desktop build game names come from the game's own Polish texts. The Polish text is a first draft and has not been reviewed by a native speaker yet, so expect odd wording in places.
- **New start screen on the Map tab**: a grid of big icon cells for the common actions, your 3 most recent files as pills, a What's new button, and the version and author under the title. The shortcut keys for the start screen cells are configurable.
- Closing the Map Grid now goes back to the start screen, even with a map loaded. Closing Random Map returns to the Map tab.
- Norwegian now says "rute" instead of "flis" for a map tile.

See [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/mimiasei/map-editor-json-tool/compare/v0.9.5-6...v0.9.5-7) for what changed.

### What's new since 0.9.5-5

- **The editor can now be used in other languages**: English, French, German, Ukrainian, Russian and Norwegian. Pick the interface language in the Theme editor. Menus, dialogs, tooltips, guides, templates and the native menu bar follow it, and on the desktop build hero, creature, artifact and object names come from the game's own texts for that language. The French, German, Ukrainian, Russian and Norwegian texts are first drafts and have not been reviewed by native speakers yet, so expect odd wording in places. Condition/action names, ids and everything saved into maps stay English.
- **New toolbar**: a Map | Quests switch at the left picks the view, and every tool is now an icon with a tooltip (same style as the Map Grid tools). Map shows the map tools (New Map, Random Map, Fairness, ...); Quests shows the quest tools (Template, Script templates, Story, Publish, Event timeline, Quest flow, ...). Undo, Redo, Validate, Guides, Game DB, Search, Statistics and More are in both. Opening a map lands in the Map view. "Export" is now called "Save As" (web build).
- **Map Grid water has a colour per water type** (Grass, Dirt, Fallen, Death, Sand, Snow, Lava), and the tile info line names the water type instead of the ground under it.
- **Random maps: each lake now gets the water that matches the ground mostly bordering it**, instead of a random one (also for flooded island regions).
- **Walkables brush: Grass slider** (0-100%) for how much of what it scatters is grass. The Dirt biome now uses the same walkables as Grass.
- **Map Grid zooming is faster**: a new "Fast zoom" setting, no icons are mounted beyond the screen edge, and the custom drawing-quality sliders can be collapsed.
- **Random squads**: an example-squad preview for a squad's value, and a faction picker for existing random squads.
- More theme presets (Factions, Terrain, Relics & Artifacts). Presets you remove from the app are cleaned out of your saved themes.
- The map statistics no longer repeat the player balance (use the Fairness button).
- Clicking outside an open dropdown no longer closes the whole dialog.

See [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/mimiasei/map-editor-json-tool/compare/v0.9.5-5...v0.9.5-6) for what changed.

### What's new since 0.9.4

- **Map Grid looks much closer to the game.** Terrain uses the game's own biome ground textures (blended per biome, with a fade between neighbouring biomes), cliffs use the game's cliff pieces, ramps show as shaded slopes, and roads and rivers are drawn with the game's own pieces. Objects are rendered from the game's 3D models, and city spawners show the chosen faction's city.
- **Water**: shore fade, a translucent teal surface with ripples and glints (switch in the Map Grid settings), and water spreads over a newly lowered area connected to existing water when you release the stroke.
- **Fairness check**: a new button next to Validate scores the map with the same algorithm the random map generator uses, with recommendations, a "not compared" list and a per-player decorations section.
- **Link portals** in the Map Grid by clicking the partner portal (two-way, with unlink). Not yet verified in the game.
- **Story Builder**: wizard that builds a whole story (quests, dialogs, counters, texts) from premade stories or your own idea, with an optional AI text writer (Gemini / Groq key) and offline phrase banks.
- **Quests are now saved inside the .map** (Block 4), so published maps actually run their quests in the game.
- **File > Open Recent** lists your recent maps and projects, newest first.
- **Objects can be stacked** on top of each other with a rearrangeable order; mirrored objects and objects rotated 180/270 degrees are drawn flipped.
- **Bucket-filling a Player Area** now also paints the blocked tiles of objects inside it (e.g. a city's footprint).
- Starting artifacts for custom heroes, a Hero tool for placing random heroes, Actions Before/After editing for zones and objects, map pickers inside the Map Grid, and a Duplicate button on actions.
- Random map generator: max heroes per player setting, and it remembers your last settings.
- Map Grid: drawing quality setting, object browser Size filter and Reset all, a banner when painting Player Areas while they are hidden in settings, a styled paint toolbar with new icons, and faster edits.
- **New Walkables brush** (flower icon, right of Trees): scatters grass, flowers and mushrooms with the same biome-mix settings as Trees.
- **Trees and Obstacles brushes mix more biomes on Snow and Lava** when high-contrast biomes are off: Snow also takes Grass pine trees, Deathland and Dirt; Lava also takes Deathland and Grass. The Mountains share in Obstacles now starts at 50%.
- **The eraser removes objects while you drag**, instead of only when you release the mouse button (rivers, roads and ramps still go on release).
- **Random cities can be given an owner and a faction** in the info column. A new random city now starts with no owner ("None", as in GME) instead of becoming Player 1's when GME opens the map. "Neutral" owners are now called "None".
- **The Map Grid pans with the right mouse button**, as in GME (it was the middle button), and a banner with a progress bar shows while the terrain textures load.
- **Encounter difficulty ranges are higher** (Easy 1050-5250, Normal 5251-10500, Difficult 10501-15750, Impossible 15751-21000, Lethal 21001-50000). Ranges you have edited yourself are kept.
- **Saving no longer pops up a list of map issues**; the Validate button still lists them on demand.
- **Help > What's new** shows these notes.
- Elevation now blocks the lower ring around a raised area, as verified in the game.

See [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/mimiasei/map-editor-json-tool/compare/v0.9.4...v0.9.5-5) for what changed.

### What's new

- **H3 monsters and artifacts now convert to their real OE equivalents**, not just a generic random encounter. A specific H3 creature (e.g. a placed Griffin) becomes a real, correctly-tiered OE unit guarding the spot; a specific H3 artifact becomes the matching real OE item. Where no direct OE faction exists (Tower, Stronghold, Fortress, Conflux, and others), it nearest-matches by combat value instead. Only ever converts to a unit OE can actually place — a real, hard-won gap where one candidate looked valid but had no in-game squad entry is now avoided.
- **Every H3 external dwelling now converts correctly**, not just Castle's. Previously any dwelling belonging to another faction silently became a Castle Pikeman hut; every faction's real dwelling (and every standalone neutral one) now maps to its own real OE equivalent.
- **The map-opening "day 1" message many H3 maps use is now preserved.** H3's timed events (the mechanism behind a map's intro text, and any resources it grants) now convert into a real in-game quest and dialog, instead of being silently dropped.
- **Custom H3 town names now display correctly in-game.** They were being written as literal text into a field the game only ever treats as a lookup key — a custom-named town would have shown as raw placeholder text instead of its real name.
- **A specific monster with no explicit count in the source H3 map now gets a sensible garrison size** instead of always converting to a single unit.
- **New: detailed import report you can save to a file.** After an H3 import, a "Save report…" button writes a plain-text summary, and a companion CSV export lets you query the full per-object conversion detail (what mapped to what, and why) with any spreadsheet or database tool.
- **Fewer areas are wrongly marked impassable after import**, especially underground — the accessibility pass now uses the source map's own real terrain data as ground truth instead of only OE's post-conversion object footprints.
- 14 more H3 interactable objects (Altar of Sacrifice, Arena, Pandora Box, Fountain of Fortune, University, and others) now convert instead of being skipped.
- Player-start city spawners now carry the correct faction when the source H3 town is Castle, Rampart, Inferno, Necropolis, or Dungeon; every other town type is left as a random-faction start, matching how a manually-placed spawner already worked.
- The "Import H3 Map…" intro screen has a "Don't show this again" option.
- **Fixed a real data-leak bug affecting New Map, Import H3 Map, and Open Map alike**: opening a map no longer merges its dialogs, localization text, and custom heroes/objects with whatever the previously-open map left behind — everything is now fully cleared first.

See [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/mimiasei/map-editor-json-tool/compare/v0.9.0...v0.9.1) for what changed.

### What's new
- **Browse-mode edits now auto-save**: every field in the tile-inspector panel (faction, spawner owner, random-squad value, garrison, reward params, etc.) commits immediately instead of needing a separate "Save to .map" click that was easy to miss.
- **New Encounter tool**: places random-squad guard encounters the same way Landmark places interactables, with a difficulty picker (Random/Easy/Normal/Difficult/Impossible/Lethal — multiple can be enabled at once), a biome-mix slider, and an option to also drop a resource pickup on the tile above. Random's odds and every difficulty's value range are now tunable in the Map Grid settings' new Advanced section.
- **Clear All**: a one-click way to wipe an entire map — every object, squad, marker, river, and player-start spawner — and reset all terrain to Grass, with a confirmation step before it runs.
- **Streamlined Paint toolbar**: every tool is now icon-only, with its label rolling out on hover, so all 13 tools fit comfortably in the header instead of crowding it.
- Fixed switching from Paint to Browse mode leaving some tools (Road, Ramp, Landmark, Encounter, River, Trees) still armed, so a click in Browse mode could keep painting.
- Fixed the Encounter tool's Random difficulty over-favoring high-value ("Lethal") squads, and its rolled values landing too often near a range's floor instead of clustering around the middle.

### What's new
- **Map Grid rewrite**: the Map Grid is now an always-editable inline view instead of a modal dialog (issue #195) — every tool stages its change live while you paint or drag and only commits on an explicit Save, with a new Rectangle interaction mode, adjustable brush-size radius, and a visual brush-shape cursor preview.
- **Roads, rivers, and ramps**: paint roads (dirt/stone) and rivers straight onto the map, rendered sub-tile with optional edge shading; a new Ramp tool marks elevation transitions in all four directions.
- **Scatter brushes**: Obstacles and Trees brushes place biome-appropriate scenery with tunable mountain/pool chance and a biome-mix slider, plus a switch to allow or block visually clashing ("high-contrast") biome mixes; a new Landmark brush scatters random interactables the same way.
- **More terrain tools**: bucket-fill terrain, a Zones tool, a Level brush, Water flood-fill, and a Browse/Paint mode toggle so you can't accidentally edit while just looking around (issue #193).
- **Create New Map**: choose from many more size presets and start editing immediately — nothing is written to disk until you explicitly save, with unsaved-changes guards on New Map and on navigating away.
- **Unified Save**: Save/Save As now behaves the same for both the .map file and the scenario JSON, backed by a new in-memory document model with full-fidelity staged previews for every edit.
- **City/hero spawners**: editable player assignment, faction, and companion/own hero right on the map; random-squad encounters get an editable value field and quick difficulty buttons.
- Fixed several dialog papercuts (outside clicks closing dialogs they shouldn't) and hero-spawner footprint/passability being treated as 3×3 instead of its real 1-tile size.

### What's new
- **Map Grid**: the visual map editor (issue #167) is now feature-complete — move, add, delete, rotate, and drag-to-paint any object; paint terrain; a blocked-tile (passability) overlay with elevation shading and ramp arrows; multi-tile footprint icons; and a full Object Browser for placing objects.
- **Place real creatures/units**: the Object Browser can now place actual creature squads (not just decorative objects), with hover tooltips showing descriptions and unit stats.
- **City/hero spawners**: adding a city-spawner or hero-spawner as a real player-start point is now supported.
- **Custom buff creator** (issue #165), plus a rewritten artifact bonus editor with friendlier, non-technical fields.
- Fixed random-squad placements being invisible or uninvokable in-game due to a requestedValue/tier mismatch (confirmed against real player.log data).
- Fixed a crash when added objects reached the real game (Minimap NRE), a crash on maps whose quest data omits subQuest.triggers, and several custom object/artifact editor bugs.
- Fixed drag-to-move UI deadlock, cursor overrides, and conflicts with map panning.

### What's new
- **Custom Heroes** now have their own sidebar section, just like Custom Objects and Custom Artifacts — clone an existing hero, or build one from scratch (pick just a fraction/class type and start blank).
- **Custom Map Objects**: new "Build from scratch" mode lets you pick any object's visual independently from its native behavior, with a clickable grid for placing exactly where the interaction point sits.
- **Custom Artifacts**: added "Build from scratch" mode, plus full editing of item stats (rarity, slot, cost, etc.) and mechanical bonuses — previously only name/icon were editable.
- **Desktop app**: consolidated the header — file actions (New/Open/Save/Save As) now live only in the native File menu, and Guides/Game Database/Publish moved from the "More" menu into the toolbar. A small indicator now shows when you have changes not yet published.
- **JSON Preview** panel can now show and edit every file that actually ships with your map — custom heroes, objects, artifacts, and localization per language — not just the scenario and dialogs.
- Fixed the Game Database's Map Objects list duplicating every artifact, a raw-JSON view showing "[object Object]" instead of formatted JSON, and the Map Grid info panel not scrolling when it had a lot to show.

See [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/mimiasei/map-editor-json-tool/commits/main) for what changed.

What's new:
- Custom map objects can now have their own icon, chosen independently from the base object they were cloned from, instead of always inheriting the base object's icon.

See CHANGELOG (https://github.com/mimiasei/map-editor-json-tool/commits/main) for what changed.
